title: Growing sunflower shoots
subtitle: Thick, crunchy cotyledons from pre-soaked sunflower seed, cut in 10 to 14 days
excerpt: Sunflower shoots produce the largest and most substantial cotyledons in the microgreen range: thick, juicy stems with large flat seed leaves that have a mild nutty flavour. The large seed requires an 8-hour pre-soak before sowing.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Soaking large, hard-coated seeds (peas, sunflowers, beans) in room-temperature water for 6 to 12 hours before sowing. The water penetrates the seed coat, triggers the germination signal, and dramatically reduces the time to the first visible shoot.

Watering by setting the growing tray inside a second tray filled with water, allowing the growing medium to draw moisture up from below. Keeps the seedling surface dry and reduces mould and damping-off risk in microgreen trays.

content.text: Sunflower shoots are a year-round indoor tray crop with a 10 to 14 day cycle. The large striped seed must be pre-soaked for 8 hours before sowing; without soaking the cotyledons emerge slowly and the seed hulls stick to the seed leaves, requiring hand removal. Sow densely on a 25 cm tray after soaking, blackout for three days under a weighted cover, then move to bright light and cut when the large seed leaves are fully open. The texture is thick and slightly crunchy, the flavour mild and nutty.

Sunflower shoots are distinctly larger than other microgreens and work as a salad ingredient rather than a garnish. The seed hulls sometimes cling to the cotyledons even after soaking; a brief misting and a wait of 30 minutes usually releases them.

Light: a very bright south-facing windowsill works in spring and summer. Sunflower shoots have larger cotyledons than brassica microgreens and need more light to develop well. In winter, a grow light 15 to 20 cm above the tray at 14 to 16 hours per day is recommended. In low light the cotyledons stay partially closed and the stems are weak.
Temperature: 18 to 24°C. Sunflower germinates and grows best in slightly warmer conditions than brassicas. A warm kitchen counter away from cold drafts is ideal.
sunflower seed in room-temperature water for 8 hours. The seeds absorb water visibly; drain and rinse before sowing.

Day 0: sow. Fill a 25 cm tray with pre-dampened seed compost to within 2 cm of the rim. Spread the soaked seeds in a dense single layer, touching but not stacked. Press firmly into contact with the medium. Do not cover with soil.

Days 1 to 3: blackout. Stack a second tray on top with a substantial weight (1 to 2 kg). Sunflower shoots push up forcefully and can lift a light cover. The weight also helps the seed hulls separate from the seed leaves as the shoots push upward. Remove the cover when the shoots are 3 to 5 cm tall.
Day 4 onward: light. The large cotyledons open and green up within 24 to 48 hours.
daily: set the tray inside a second tray with 2 to 3 cm of water. Sunflower shoots are large and use more water than brassica microgreens; check daily. Remove standing water after 30 minutes.
Days 10 to 14: cut. When the cotyledons are fully open, flat, and 8 to 12 cm tall, cut 2 cm above the medium with scissors. Rinse, use fresh or refrigerate for up to two days.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common problems on sunflower shoot trays.

items.symptom: Seed hulls cling to the cotyledons after the blackout phase
items.cause: The thick sunflower hull does not always release cleanly even after soaking.
items.fix: Mist the affected cotyledons with water and wait 20 to 30 minutes; the hull softens and can be gently removed by hand. Heavier weights during the blackout phase improve hull separation on the next batch.

items.symptom: Mould on the medium surface between the seeds
items.cause: Surface moisture from standing water or poor airflow.
items.fix: Remove standing water from the outer tray promptly after bottom-watering. Run a small fan nearby. Rinse soaked seeds thoroughly before sowing to remove surface sugars.

items.symptom: Large cotyledons stay folded, don't open flat
items.cause: Insufficient light or blackout cover removed too early.
items.fix: Move to a brighter position or add a grow light. Ensure the cover is removed only once shoots are 3 to 5 cm tall; removing it earlier leaves cotyledons still folded.

items.symptom: Seeds fail to germinate after soaking
items.cause: Old seed stock or insufficient soak time.
items.fix: Use fresh sunflower seed intended for growing (food-grade sunflower seed sold for eating has sometimes been heat-treated and won't germinate). Soak for a full 8 hours.

content.text: Use untreated sunflower seed in the shell (the grey-striped seed with the hull intact). Shelled sunflower kernels (the white seeds sold as bird food or snack food) do not germinate reliably. Microgreen suppliers sell in-shell sunflower seed in quantities suited to tray growing.
